title: Medicaid community engagement requirement, federal floor from January 1, 2027
source: P.L. 119-21 section 71119 and the CMS interim final rule CMS-2454-IFC (June 2026), as summarized by KFF, SHVS and CHCS. States may add details; check your state's rules before any live use.

requirement.plain_language: Starting in January 2027, most adults aged 19 to 64 on Medicaid need to show 80 hours a month of work, school, volunteering, or a job training program, or earn about 580 dollars a month, to keep their coverage. Some people are exempt.
requirement.awareness_question: Before this call, had you heard about the new Medicaid rule about work hours that starts in January?
requirement.hours_question: In a typical month, about how many hours do you work, go to school, volunteer, or take part in a job training program? A rough number is fine.
requirement.income_question: Do you earn more or less than about 580 dollars a month before taxes?
checklist_meets: Report your hours or income to the state before your coverage check date.
Keep recent pay stubs, a school schedule, or a volunteer letter in case the state asks.
checklist_at_risk: A free navigator can help you find volunteering or job training that counts toward the 80 hours.
Tell the state if anything changes, such as a new job, a pregnancy, or caring for someone.

exemptions.label: Parent or caregiver of a child 13 or younger
exemptions.question: Do you take care of a child who is 13 or younger?
checklist: Tell the state the name and age of the child you care for.
Keep a school or birth record in case the state asks.

exemptions.label: Pregnant or gave birth in the last year
exemptions.question: Are you pregnant right now, or have you had a baby in the last year?
checklist: Tell the state you are pregnant or recently gave birth.
Keep a note from your clinic with your due date or delivery date in case the state asks.

exemptions.label: Caregiver of a person with a disability
exemptions.question: Do you take care of someone with a disability, like a parent or another family member?
checklist: Tell the state who you care for.
Keep a doctor's letter or proof of their disability benefits in case the state asks.

exemptions.label: Medically frail: a condition that limits daily activities
exemptions.question: Do you have a health condition, a disability, or a mental health or substance use condition?
exemptions.follow_up: Does it make it hard for you to work or to do everyday things, like getting dressed, shopping, or getting around?
checklist: Ask your doctor or clinic to confirm that your condition limits your daily activities.
Tell the state you are asking for the medically frail exemption.

exemptions.label: Gets SNAP or TANF and meets their work rules
exemptions.question: Do you get SNAP food benefits or TANF cash assistance?
checklist: Give the state your SNAP or TANF case number; the state can usually confirm this itself.

exemptions.label: Veteran with a total disability rating
exemptions.question: Are you a veteran with a total disability rating from the VA?
checklist: Keep your VA disability rating letter.

exemptions.label: In a drug or alcohol treatment program
exemptions.question: Are you in a drug or alcohol treatment program right now?
checklist: Ask your treatment program for a letter confirming you are enrolled.

exemptions.label: Former foster youth under 26
exemptions.question: Were you in foster care when you turned 18?
checklist: Tell the state you were in foster care at 18; the state can usually confirm this itself.

exemptions.label: American Indian or Alaska Native
exemptions.note: Taken from state records only. Never asked on a call.
checklist: No action needed if the state's records already show this.
